note: Directional heuristics only. Each rule adds a delta to a profile key; the interpreter clamps to the edit bounds. Deltas are deliberately small so one roast can attribute the effect.

rules.why: low density (<650 g/L): less thermal mass, so a gentler start avoids scorching the surface before the interior catches up
high density (>=750 g/L): more thermal mass and lower conductivity, so more energy early keeps the curve on target
high moisture (>11.5%): more energy is spent drying, so push the drying phase harder
low moisture (<9.5%): dries fast, so hold back energy to avoid a runaway early rise
grown at >=1500 m: denser, slower to conduct heat, so add energy
natural/honey/anaerobic: more sugars on the surface, so ease the early heat to avoid tipping
washed: clean surface, tolerates a stronger early curve

load.why: load differs from the profile's reference weight: the same curve needs proportionally more or less energy
